feasible.reason: The SRAM half of the threat is real and the fix is sound and cheap under every pq1 constraint. Verified in-repo: `secure/src/ui/lcd.rs:104/111/264/277` — `cell: [u16; CELL_N]` is a persistent static scratch that `blit_glyph` fills with secret glyph pixels on the `flush_with_secret_rows` path and never clears; `secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs:55/309-322` — `static mut STRIP` receives the secret-cell pixels on a forced frame and only `SHOWN` is invalidated (digest never recorded, good) — STRIP itself is never zeroed; `seed_wizard.rs:584-612` and `1027-1040` — `secret_rows_storage`/`wb` are stack locals with no `zeroize()`, while the px twin `px_mnemonic_page` (`seed_wizard.rs:96-100`) DOES `c.zeroize()` — so 'the px twins already do' is accurate for the wizard cells, but NOT for the pixel buffer (`STRIP`) which no path zeroizes. `grep zeroize` over `secure/src/ui/px/*.rs` and `pqsigner-ui-px/src/*.rs` returns nothing. Threat model fit: NS cannot read S-SRAM, so this is defence-in-depth against a future secure-world bug / post-lock dump, not a current exploit — correctly rated as parity + P1 only if the project treats pixel-form seed residue as equal to byte-form residue (it does for every other secret type via `ZeroizeOnDrop`). Feasibility: `fi::zeroize_barrier()` (`fi.rs:290`) already provides the compiler_fence+DSB discipline; zeroizing ~15 KB of statics per forced frame is microseconds at 160 MHz; no flash cost that matters against the 76,949 B overage (tens of bytes). Backlight-off on pq1 is realisable: `LCM_EN` PB15 is secure-owned (`board/pq1.rs:118`, `sau.rs` secures I2C2 and UCPD1 so NS cannot flip it), and `aw99703::configure()/enable()` already exist for re-enable. `hard_reset()` exists and `LCD_RST_IS_DRIVABLE = true` on pq1 (`board/pq1.rs:113`). Kind=firmware is correct — no hardware change needed. Cost S is right.
feasible.corrections:
1. THE GRAM-RESIDUE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED. On the legacy path, `show_status("Words shown")` → `Display::flush()` repaints ALL 64 glyph cells (comment at `lcd.rs:148-153`: 'draw_line space-pads every row to 16 cols, so all 64 cells are overwritten'), and secret glyphs only ever land in those same 64 cells (inter-cell gaps never hold secret ink). So after the wizard exits the GRAM no longer holds secret glyphs on the legacy path. On the px path a forced frame runs `invalidate_shown()`, so the very next status frame blits every strip (`present_frame_ex` iterates y0 over 0..H) — again the whole GRAM is overwritten. The real GRAM window is only: (a) power-cut / MCU reset while a secret page is on glass (GRAM survives an MCU reset while the panel stays powered — but the FSBL's `nv3007` init clears the panel, `fsbl/src/render.rs:95`), and (b) the idle-timeout / tamper wipe firing DURING the wizard without a repaint. Re-scope the threat to those windows; `fill_screen(BG)` on lock/wipe then becomes cheap belt-and-braces (24 ms at 40 MHz per the `fill_rect` comment, not 20 ms), not the primary fix.
2. 'PULSE THE PANEL RESET SO GRAM IS CLEARED IN HARDWARE' IS NOT A GRAM-CLEARING MECHANISM. ST7789-class controllers (NV3007 is the same family) specify frame memory as 'no change' on both H/W and S/W reset — only power-on leaves it random. Nothing in `lcd_nv3007.rs` or `docs/hardware/nv3007*.md` evidences otherwise. A reset also forces the full re-init sequence (`hard_reset` alone is 330 ms of delays plus `run_init_sequence`). Drop the reset step; `fill_screen(BG)` (write-only, no MISO needed) is the only reliable GRAM eraser. Backlight-off (AW99703 HWEN low) HIDES but does not erase — state that honestly.
3. GRAM READ-BACK IS NOT POSSIBLE FROM THE BOARD: pq1 has no MISO (`LCD_MISO_PIN = None`, `board/pq1.rs:103`), so a RAMRD oracle requires tapping the panel FPC physically. The GRAM threat is therefore physical-only; P1 for the SRAM half, P2 for the GRAM half.
4. HOST TEST (3) CANNOT LIVE WHERE THE BUFFERS LIVE. `mod ui` is `#[cfg(not(test))]` in `secure/src/main.rs:282-283` and `STRIP` is a `static mut` inside `secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs`, so a test written there NEVER runs (known trap — see memory 'secure/src modules excluded from host tests'). The strip-zeroing must be moved into `pqsigner-ui-px` (e.g. a `Strip::finish_secret()` / `ZeroizeOnDrop` on the strip buffer in `raster.rs`) so the all-zero-after-forced-frame assertion runs in that crate's `tests/`. The legacy `cell` buffer has no host-testable twin at all; its test would need a `secure-miri-tests`-style harness or a pure helper in `shared/`.
5. ZEROIZE TARGET VALUE: `cell` should be refilled with `BG` (= 0x0000, `lcd.rs:48`) — identical to zero here, but document it so a future non-black BG does not reintroduce a non-zero 'clean' value that still differs from the secret pattern.
6. IDLE-TIMEOUT PATH: `zeroize_sensitive_state()` (`nsc/mod.rs:1729`) paints nothing; the display is only repainted because the wizard/PendSV path restarts PIN entry (`main.rs:943-944`). Hook the `fill_screen(BG)` + buffer zeroize INTO `zeroize_sensitive_state()` so every caller (CMD_LOCK, idle, tamper, panic) gets it, rather than adding it to each site.
7. CELL ZEROIZE FREQUENCY: zeroizing `cell` after EACH secret glyph (48 blits per page) is unnecessary — once at the end of `flush_with_secret_rows` suffices, since the same buffer is overwritten by the next blit anyway; what matters is that no secret pattern remains after the LAST blit.

The 'clears on init' claim is true only for the ltdc_dsi driver (T3W1): ltdc_dsi/display_fb.c:185-194. More importantly, no Trezor Core path clears FBs or zeroizes secret text on lock/idle/wipe: `lock_device` → `run_lockscreen` merely renders a new layout (core/src/apps/homescreen/__init__.py:83-95) and fades the backlight (core/src/trezor/ui/__init__.py:254-255); `grep zeroize core/embed/rust/src/ui` is empty and ShareWords holds `TString` refs (layout_delizia/component/share_words.rs:23-24).
